# OSHA's Form 301 (Rev. 04/2004)

Injury and Illness

Incident Report

This Injury and Illness Incident Report is one of the first forms you must fill out when a recordable work-related injury or illness has occurred. Together with the Logof Work-Related Injuries and Inesses and the accompanying Summary, these forms help the employer and OSHA develop a picture of the extent and severity of work-related incidents.

Within 7 calendar days after you receive information that a recordable work-related injury or illness has occurred, you must fill out this form or an

sequivalent. Some state workers' compensation: weinsurance or other reports may be acceptable

substitutes. To be considered an equivalent form, any substitute must contain all the information asked for on this form.

- Name of physician or other health care professional David Cochran
- If treatment was given away from the v Facility Brown-Miller

According to Public Law 91-596 and 29 CFR 1904, OSHA's recordkeeping rule, you must keep this form on file for 5 years following the year to which it pertains.

If you need additional copies of this form, you may photocopy the printout or insert additional form pages in the PDF, and then use as many as you need.

- + What object or substance directly harmed the employee? Examples: "concrete floor": "chlorine" "radial arm saw." If this question does not apply to the incident, leave it blank. Santiago
- If the employee died, when did death occur?
